Presidential bid by leader of far-right National Rally has no shortage of supporters in scenic Montargis In the small French town of Montargis, Jean-Antoine, a retired decorator, was pleased Marine Le Pen had again shaken up French politics by launching a bid for the presidency, despite her legal woes. “Even the judges said she didn’t personally profit from the money, it was for her party,” he said of Le Pen’s newly upheld conviction for embezzlement. “All politicians in France have always been schemers, it’s just a fact of life.” Jean-Antoine, 76, who once painted luxury fashion stores, felt voters for the figurehead of France’s far-right, anti-immigration party National Rally (RN) wouldn’t care about this week’s appeal court decision over Le Pen’s misuse of European parliament funds.

In the small French town of Montargis, Jean-Antoine, a retired decorator, was pleased Marine Le Pen had again shaken up French politics by launching a bid for the presidency, despite her legal woes. “Even the judges said she didn’t personally profit from the money, it was for her party,” he said of Le Pen’s newly upheld conviction for embezzlement. “All politicians in France have always been schemers, it’s just a fact of life.” Jean-Antoine, 76, who once painted luxury fashion stores, felt voters for the figurehead of France’s far-right, anti-immigration party National Rally (RN) wouldn’t care about this week’s appeal court decision over Le Pen’s misuse of European parliament funds.

Jean-Antoine’s late father fled to France from Spain during its civil war in the 1930s and became part of the French resistance standing up to occupation by Hitler’s Germany. “But now immigration has to stop,” he said. Le Pen’s conviction last year had meant she was barred from running for office until the 2030s, but that restriction was shortened by appeal judges this week. This allowed her to declare a phoenix-like return to the presidential race, which will be voted on next year. The court’s decision came despite its ruling that she was guilty of playing a key part in siphoning off of more than €2.8m through a fake-jobs scam of unprecedented scale and duration, and funnelling it to her cash-strapped party between 2004 and 2016.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World]
Presidential bid by leader of far-right National Rally has no shortage of supporters in scenic Montargis

In the small French town of Montargis, Jean-Antoine, a retired decorator, was pleased Marine Le Pen had again shaken up French politics by launching a bid for the presidency, despite her legal woes.

“Even the judges said she didn’t personally profit from the money, it was for her party,” he said of Le Pen’s newly upheld conviction for embezzlement. “All politicians in France have always been schemers, it’s just a fact of life.”

Jean-Antoine, 76, who once painted luxury fashion stores, felt voters for the figurehead of France’s far-right, anti-immigration party National Rally (RN) wouldn’t care about this week’s appeal court decision over Le Pen’s misuse of European parliament funds.

Jean-Antoine’s late father fled to France from Spain during its civil war in the 1930s and became part of the French resistance standing up to occupation by Hitler’s Germany. “But now immigration has to stop,” he said.

Le Pen’s conviction last year had meant she was barred from running for office until the 2030s, but that restriction was shortened by appeal judges this week. This allowed her to declare a phoenix-like return to the presidential race, which will be voted on next year.

The court’s decision came despite its ruling that she was guilty of playing a key part in siphoning off of more than €2.8m through a fake-jobs scam of unprecedented scale and duration, and funnelling it to her cash-strapped party between 2004 and 2016.

Judges ordered her to wear an electronic ankle tag for one year with a curfew at her home, but she has vowed to lodge an appeal with France’s highest court, which will effectively put her conviction and sentence on hold while she campaigns ahead of the presidential vote. Snap polling this week showed her popularity is high and she is in a strong position for the two-round vote next April and May. She previously lost to Emmanuel Macron in 2017 and 2022.

Montargis, 75 miles south of Paris, is known for its scenic canals and its pralines. It is one of many towns that elected rightwing mayors in local elections earlier this year, when RN and its allies more than tripled the number of town halls under their control.

“When they won here, I went to the town hall and I said: ‘I don’t know if you can do any better than the last lot but you can’t do any worse,’” said Jean-Antoine. “And that’s what I’d say to Marine Le Pen. People want change.”

payload.title: Marine Le Pen palasi presidenttikilpaan tuomiosta huolimatta
payload.summary: Marine Le Pen voi tavoitella Ranskan presidentin tehtävää, koska muutoksenhakutuomioistuin lyhensi hänen vaalikelpoisuuttaan rajoittanutta kieltoa. Montargis’ssa haastateltu kannattaja ei pitänyt tuomiota esteenä Le Penin tukemiselle.
payload.content:
Ranskan laitaoikeistolaisen Kansallisen liittouman johtohahmo Marine Le Pen on ilmoittanut palaavansa presidenttikilpaan, vaikka muutoksenhakutuomioistuin piti voimassa hänen tuomionsa Euroopan parlamentin varojen väärinkäytöstä. Ehdokkuuden mahdollisti se, että tuomioistuin lyhensi aiemmin määrättyä vaalikelpoisuuden rajoitusta. Ranskan seuraavat presidentinvaalit järjestetään ensi vuonna.

## Vaalikelpoisuuden rajoitusta lyhennettiin

Le Penin viime vuonna saama tuomio olisi alkuperäisessä muodossaan estänyt häntä asettumasta ehdolle aina 2030-luvulle saakka. Tällä viikolla annettu muutoksenhakutuomioistuimen ratkaisu lyhensi kieltoa niin, että hän voi osallistua seuraaviin presidentinvaaleihin. Päätöksen jälkeen Le Pen ilmoitti paluustaan vaalikilpaan oikeudellisista vaikeuksistaan huolimatta.

Tuomioistuin katsoi Le Penin olleen keskeisessä asemassa järjestelyssä, jossa Euroopan parlamentin varoja ohjattiin yli 2,8 miljoonaa euroa hänen talousvaikeuksissa olleelle puolueelleen. Vuosina 2004–2016 toteutettu järjestely perustui tekaistuihin työpaikkoihin. Oikeus piti järjestelyä mittakaavaltaan ja kestoltaan poikkeuksellisena. Tuomio jäi siis voimaan, vaikka sen vaalikelpoisuutta koskevaa seurausta lievennettiin.

## Kannattaja puolustaa Le Peniä Montargis’ssa

Montargis’n pikkukaupungissa 76-vuotias Jean-Antoine suhtautui Le Penin paluuseen tyytyväisesti. Eläkkeellä oleva sisustustyöntekijä, joka oli aiemmin maalannut ylellisiä muotiliikkeitä, arvioi, etteivät Kansallisen liittouman äänestäjät välitä oikeuden päätöksestä. Kansallinen liittouma tunnetaan laitaoikeistolaisena ja maahanmuuttovastaisena puolueena.

Jean-Antoine korosti, etteivät rahat hänen käsityksensä mukaan tulleet Le Penin henkilökohtaiseen käyttöön, vaan päätyivät puolueelle. Hän suhtautui tapaukseen kyynisesti ja sanoi poliitikkojen juonitelleen Ranskassa aina. Näkemys kuvastaa sitä, ettei hän pitänyt varojen väärinkäyttöä ratkaisevana syynä luopua Le Penin kannattamisesta.

Jean-Antoinen perhetausta tuo hänen maahanmuuttokantaansa huomionarvoisen vastakohdan. Hänen edesmennyt isänsä pakeni Espanjan sisällissotaa Ranskaan 1930-luvulla ja liittyi myöhemmin Hitlerin Saksan miehitystä vastustaneeseen Ranskan vastarintaliikkeeseen. Jean-Antoine sanoi tästä huolimatta, että maahanmuuton on nyt loputtava. Le Penin lyhennetty vaalikielto antaa hänen kaltaistensa kannattajien äänestää puolueen johtohahmoa jo ensi vuoden presidentinvaaleissa.
summary_bullets: Muutoksenhakutuomioistuin piti Le Penin tuomion voimassa mutta lyhensi hänen vaalikelpoisuuttaan rajoittanutta kieltoa.
Ratkaisu mahdollistaa Le Penin osallistumisen ensi vuoden presidentinvaaleihin.
Montargis’ssa haastateltu kannattaja ei pitänyt varojen väärinkäyttöä esteenä Le Penin tukemiselle.

Näkemys kuvastaa sitä, ettei hän pitänyt varojen väärinkäyttöä ratkaisevana syynä luopua Le Penin kannattamisesta.

Jean-Antoinen perhetausta tuo hänen maahanmuuttokantaansa huomionarvoisen vastakohdan. Hänen edesmennyt isänsä pakeni Espanjan sisällissotaa Ranskaan 1930-luvulla ja liittyi myöhemmin Hitlerin Saksan miehitystä vastustaneeseen Ranskan vastarintaliikkeeseen. Jean-Antoine sanoi tästä huolimatta, että maahanmuuton on nyt loputtava. Le Penin lyhennetty vaalikielto antaa hänen kaltaistensa kannattajien äänestää puolueen johtohahmoa jo ensi vuoden presidentinvaaleissa.

Presidential bid by leader of far-right National Rally has no shortage of supporters in scenic Montargis In the small French town of Montargis, Jean-Antoine, a retired decorator, was pleased Marine Le Pen had again shaken up French politics by launching a bid for the presidency, despite her legal woes. “Even the judges said she didn’t personally profit from the money, it was for her party,” he said of Le Pen’s newly upheld conviction for embezzlement. “All politicians in France have always been schemers, it’s just a fact of life.” Jean-Antoine, 76, who once painted luxury fashion stores, felt voters for the figurehead of France’s far-right, anti-immigration party National Rally (RN) wouldn’t care about this week’s appeal court decision over Le Pen’s misuse of European parliament funds.

In the small French town of Montargis, Jean-Antoine, a retired decorator, was pleased Marine Le Pen had again shaken up French politics by launching a bid for the presidency, despite her legal woes. “Even the judges said she didn’t personally profit from the money, it was for her party,” he said of Le Pen’s newly upheld conviction for embezzlement. “All politicians in France have always been schemers, it’s just a fact of life.” Jean-Antoine, 76, who once painted luxury fashion stores, felt voters for the figurehead of France’s far-right, anti-immigration party National Rally (RN) wouldn’t care about this week’s appeal court decision over Le Pen’s misuse of European parliament funds.

Jean-Antoine’s late father fled to France from Spain during its civil war in the 1930s and became part of the French resistance standing up to occupation by Hitler’s Germany. “But now immigration has to stop,” he said. Le Pen’s conviction last year had meant she was barred from running for office until the 2030s, but that restriction was shortened by appeal judges this week. This allowed her to declare a phoenix-like return to the presidential race, which will be voted on next year. The court’s decision came despite its ruling that she was guilty of playing a key part in siphoning off of more than €2.8m through a fake-jobs scam of unprecedented scale and duration, and funnelling it to her cash-strapped party between 2004 and 2016.
